stem: A child has a normal renal ultrasound, and a junior doctor says this makes significant cortical defects unlikely; what is the most accurate reply?

options.text: That is correct because ultrasound is more sensitive than DMSA for cortical defects
That is incorrect because DMSA is more sensitive than renal ultrasound for cortical defects and scarring
That is incorrect because abdominal X-ray is the most sensitive test for cortical defects
That is correct because DTPA is the best cortical imaging study
That is correct because MAG3 and ultrasound have equivalent sensitivity for cortical scarring

explanation: DMSA is more sensitive than renal ultrasound for cortical defects and scarring. A normal renal ultrasound does not exclude cortical abnormality as reliably as DMSA.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: DMSA (Dimercaptosuccinic acid) Scan

rationale: DMSA is the preferred test for detecting cortical defects and scarring, so a normal ultrasound does not rule them out.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because DMSA is more sensitive than renal ultrasound for cortical defects and scarring.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because DMSA is more sensitive than renal ultrasound for cortical defects and scarring.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because abdominal X-ray is not the most sensitive test for cortical defects.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because DTPA is used for GFR measurement, not cortical defect detection.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because MAG3 and ultrasound are not equivalent for cortical scarring, and DMSA is the key modality for cortical defects.
